lines.text: Do you know how speakeasies worked? Secret bars, hidden in plain sight, behind a door with no sign.
From 1920 to 1933, selling alcohol was banned across the United States. So drinking moved underground.
You'd knock on a plain door. A little slot slid open, and a pair of eyes looked you over.
No password? No entry. Even the name is a warning. Speak easy. Keep your voice down.
Inside, there were tricks everywhere. Buzzers to warn of a raid, and shelves that hid whole rooms. New York's 21 Club kept its wine behind a secret door in a brick wall.
In New York alone, there were thousands of them.
Orbi Spaces work a bit like that. A Space needs a passcode to join, its files never show up in public, and only members can open them.
